title: Consistent Hashing and Random Trees: Distributed Caching Protocols for Relieving Hot Spots on the World Wide Web
authors: David Karger, Eric Lehman, Tom Leighton, Matthew Levine, Daniel Lewin, Rina Panigrahy
finding: Consistent hashing limits reassignment when the cache membership changes. The paper also develops random cache trees to relieve hot spots under explicit theoretical models.
limit: Stable assignment alone does not split a very popular object's requests across servers. Its modeled guarantees are not a measured latency guarantee for this Go implementation.
application: Use consistent hashing as the locality baseline. Measure request imbalance and key remapping separately from cache hit ratio. Compare it to deterministic round robin on identical traces.

title: Consistent Hashing with Bounded Loads
authors: Vahab Mirrokni, Mikkel Thorup, Morteza Zadimoghaddam
venue: SODA 2018, pp. 587-604 (expanded arXiv preprint first uploaded in 2016)
finding: The allocation algorithm bounds balls per bin by ceil(c*m/n), where c is greater than one. It studies the tradeoff between balance and movement as clients or servers change.
limit: The bound concerns object/client allocation counts. Requests with unequal popularity, service times, and response sizes require another load model.
application: Study how much locality to retain before redirecting a request. MiniCDN uses in-flight request counts with a slack threshold. This is an experimental heuristic inspired by the tradeoff, not an implementation of this theorem.

title: Revisiting Consistent Hashing with Bounded Loads
authors: John Chen, Benjamin Coleman, Anshumali Shrivastava
finding: The authors identify cascaded overflow in capacity-constrained hashing and propose a method using fast minwise hashing. Evaluation includes AOL search and Indiana University click traces.
limit: The method's object placement and datasets differ from live HTTP request routing. A small synthetic demonstration cannot reproduce its empirical claims.
application: Avoid assuming clockwise overflow always balances load. Record destination distribution and locality loss. Keep minwise object allocation as a separate future baseline rather than labeling our least-loaded fallback as this algorithm.

title: Cache-aware load balancing of data center applications
authors: Aaron Archer, Kevin Aydin, MohammadHossein Bateni, Vahab Mirrokni, Aaron Schild, Ray Yang, Richard Zhuang
venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment 12(6), pp. 709-723
finding: The Google search system combines query-term locality with load balancing through weighted voting, graph partitioning, and cache simulation. The production evaluation reports fewer cache misses and increased throughput.
limit: A multi-term search query uses multiple cached posting lists. MiniCDN currently maps one HTTP resource per request, so directly transplanting the voting scheme would be unjustified.
application: Evaluate cache locality together with request balance. Report origin attempts and latency beside per-edge request counts. A more even distribution may incur additional cold fills.

title: Optimal Probabilistic Cache Stampede Prevention
authors: Andrea Vattani, Flavio Chierichetti, Keegan Lowenstein
venue: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment 8(8), pp. 886-897
finding: The paper analyzes probabilistic early refresh to reduce stampedes around cache expiration, including dependence on regeneration time.
limit: Early refresh differs from suppressing duplicate simultaneous cache fills. Extra refresh traffic must respect the origin's freshness rules and capacity.
application: Use cache-fill coordination as an implemented baseline. Treat probabilistic early refresh as a later controlled experiment, measuring origin requests, user latency, and wasted refreshes. Do not claim current coordination implements this paper.
